newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fortis '96 net seen up 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: Fortis '96 net seen up 16 pct.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis is expected to announce a 1996 net profit rise of 16 percent to some 732 million ECU from 631 million ECU on Wednesday, analysts said.

They said that the cyclical non-life insurance activities were expected to show a recovery, after the company swung to a 23 million ECU operating loss for accident and health insurance in the fourth quarter of 1995. Motor and car insurance were also expected to show better results.
Analysts said that the group's life insurance business should show another steady growth figure.
The Dutch parent company Fortis Amev is expected to announce an increase in 1996 net profits of 16.4 percent to around 806 million guilders versus 693 million guilders in the previous year.
Analysts said the Fortis Amev dividend was expected to be set between 1.84-1.94 guilders per share from 1.68 guilders in 1995.
The Belgian parent Fortis AG was expected to show an increase in net profits to 13.0 billion Belgian francs from 11.2 billion in 1995. This represents an increase of just over 16 percent.
Analysts said the 1996 dividend was expected to be around 94 Belgian francs versus 84 francs in 1995.
They said that the Belgian operations and the Dutch insurance activities were expected to show strong results.

"Only the Dutch bank activities are achieving less strong results than their competitors," said analyst Dennis Ederzeel of Delta Lloyd Bank as VSB did not have a market position as solid as for instance ABN AMRO and ING.
The recently acquired Dutch merchant bank MeesPierson was not yet consolidated in the group's 1996 results, but will be taken into account from 1997.
